An ordinary one-dimensional calculus lemma with its own quantified hypotheses. It applies to toy curves as well as diffusion moments and carries no minimizer, PDE or stochastic premise. Strict convexity gives q′(t) below its endpoint chord for r<t<s; the chord is at most one, and continuity makes the integrated deficit strictly positive. The source uses this step inside a conditional full-support argument. This node does not assert a newly extracted Lean declaration or independently accepted formal check.

Authored fixed-time consequence of smooth finite-step coercivity and compact-strip spatial-moment convergence. The ordinary proof flattens gamma locally; the inspected SKSupport source instead uses sampled jets along its canonical diffusion. actual_coercivity takes t:Time with 0<t and ContinuousAt gamma.val t and proves the scaled c^4/c^2 polynomial inequality. Its type does not require c>0; positivity is needed here to divide by c^2. This source correspondence does not identify the SKSupport and SKValue models, pass third time derivatives through a shrinking-plateau limit, or establish the smooth-density corollary as an exported formal conclusion. support_boundary.meaning: Not mapped as a claim means absent from the selected passages' claim_ids, not absent from their prose. Explicit assumption references and all recorded prerequisites are retained. No sentence-level explanation coverage is inferred.

paper_scope.meaning: Authored focus; mentioned claims and retained prerequisites may extend beyond these goals.

coverage.heading_syntax: ATX headings only; Setext and HTML headings are not parsed
coverage.scope: Mapped passages are correspondences, not sentence-level formal support. Section-passage overlaps are document structure, not claim or proof implications. Unmapped text and passages omitted by the selector remain in the validated paper. Graph records outside the selected prerequisite closure remain in the bundle and are not asserted absent. Argument links combine recorded Lean references, curated support, formalization correspondence and explicit assumptions; their SCCs describe only that mixed recorded reachability. Reading order and platform decomposition are separate.

passages.text: This AI-assisted article reconstructs the cited analytic arguments. The integrated estimate (5), its shape hypotheses and compact-strip approximation are substantial imported inputs. The [full-support formal statement][support-challenge] asserts the support and moment conclusions conditional on an admissible minimiser, and constructs its associated diffusion. A separate [scalar formal statement][value-challenge] covers value identities and finite Gaussian approximation, with minimiser and diffusion premises for those clauses. Its third clause identifies the ground-state and Parisi values from a minimiser, constructing the diffusion internally. The two formal models have not been transported into one another in this record. Neither statement includes the positive-density corollary or QAOA convergence. Their [full-support][support-lean] and [scalar][value-lean] implementations use [Lean][Lean4] and [mathlib][mathlib]. Acceptance by Comparator and extraction of the selected formal statements remain unknown. Source inspection alone establishes neither. Exact versions, checking outcomes and correspondence are retained in the long record's [§12, “What the formal statements establish”](../long/reasoning-record.md#formal-interfaces) and [§13, “Source checks and finite calculation”](../long/reasoning-record.md#verification).
passages.rationale: Source inspection of SKValue Main.lean and GroundState/MainConclusions.lean confirms that the first two clauses take a diffusion premise and the third constructs one internally. The two formal models remain untransported, neither endpoint includes positive density or QAOA, and Comparator/research-target acceptance remains unestablished. Long §§12 and 13 are linked; the unrendered source review is identified by its actual title/date rather than a nonexistent PDF.
